刮瓜具有清脆明亮的音色質感，帶有輕快活潑的特性。其音域屬於中高頻範圍，發出的聲響: The güiro has a crisp, bright timbre, light and lively in character. Its range sits in the upper middle frequencies, and what it puts into the air is dry and penetrating. Drawn up and down its notched surface with a wooden or plastic stick, it produces a clearly granular, sandy rasp with a strong sense of rhythm. Its colour falls between the metallic ring of a tambourine and the dry woodiness of a wooden fish, but with more layers to it. The resonance comes mainly from the hollow gourd-shaped body, which gives the sound a moderate spread. In an ensemble this scraped timbre creates a Latin flavour and drives the rhythm, and it complements the conga and the bongo well.
刮瓜屬體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 112.23，常見於拉丁: The güiro is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 112.23, common in Latin America and the Caribbean. Its development can be traced to South America; the Aztecs had an early relative, the omitzicahuastli, made from a small serrated bone and played in the same way. The Taíno of the Caribbean are regarded as the source of the modern güiro: Taíno people in the Dominican Republic, Cuba and Puerto Rico developed the güajey, cut with ridges from a long gourd or an animal bone. Africa also has scraped instruments of bone; Blench (2009) links the güiro to scraped idiophones in Cameroon and in West and Central Africa, and the Berom of Nigeria have the gwák or gwàshák. Modern variants also exist in metal, and in forms combined with a shaker.
刮瓜常見於古巴、波多黎各與拉丁美洲音樂，在頌樂、特羅瓦、薩爾薩的典型節奏組中扮演: The güiro is common in Cuban, Puerto Rican and Latin American music. It plays an important part in the typical rhythm sections of son, trova and salsa, and it is also used in traditional and folk dance, by dance companies and at religious festivals. The source mentions Maya dances of the Yucatán Peninsula, the Cuban danzón, Puerto Rican jíbaro music with plena, seis and danza, Caribbean coastal cumbia, Panamanian folk dance and cumbia. In the classical repertoire it appears in Villa-Lobos's Uirapuru (the score calls for a reco-reco), Gould's Latin-American Symphonette, Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring, and the intermezzo and finale of Shchedrin's Carmen Suite, a ballet adapted from Bizet's opera.
刮瓜為體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 112.23，常見於拉丁: The güiro is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 112.23, common in Latin America and the Caribbean. The traditional body is made from a dried gourd, hollow and open at one end, cut on the surface with parallel ridges; modern bodies are also made from other fruits, from wood, from synthetic fibre or from metal. The body itself is the sound source, sounding through the friction of the scraper against the ridges. It is usually played by scraping a short wooden stick back and forth; a metal variant has parallel ridges all over the outside, is rubbed with a metal scraper or stick, and is sealed with iron sand inside. The source does not state the materials of the remaining fixed parts.
刮瓜（güiro，台灣又稱刮葫或刮壺）是拉丁美洲與加勒比海的體鳴打擊樂器，霍恩博: The güiro (in Taiwan also called gua-hu, scraped gourd or scraped pot) is an idiophone percussion instrument of Latin America and the Caribbean, Hornbostel–Sachs number 112.23. Its body is usually a hollow fruit, or made of wood, synthetic fibre or metal, cut on the surface with parallel ridges; the player scrapes a short stick or a toothed scraper back and forth across the ridges, producing a continuous, short rasp. It is common in traditional folk dance, by dance companies and at religious festivals, and it also appears in Latin American rhythm sections.

演奏刮瓜時，可將手指插入器身指孔以固定樂器，再以短木棒或擦棒沿表面平行凹凸坑紋來: To play the güiro, hook your fingers through the holes in the body to hold it steady, then scrape a short wooden stick or scraper back and forth along the parallel ridges. Begin with up-and-down strokes and long and short scrapes, so that the sound moves between continuous and clipped; on a metal güiro you rub the ridges on the outside with a metal scraper or stick. The point is to keep the body steady and the scraper flat against the ridges, so that friction produces the rhythmic sound.
